title: Transcranial Temporal Interference Modulation in Parkinson's Disease for an Exploratory Study of Motor Skills (as Part of a Proof-of-Concept Study)
summary: This study examines the effect of repeated noninvasive deep brain stimulation on motor skills in patients with Parkinson’s disease. In Parkinson’s disease, a lack of neurotransmitters in the brain leads to dysfunction and dysregulation of nerve cells, which can result in, among other things, the motor symptoms of the disease, such as tremors or rigidity. There are already various therapeutic approaches to improve symptoms, consisting primarily of medication in combination with physical, occupational, and speech therapy, as well as the option of deep brain stimulation. Currently, the electrodes used for brain stimulation are implanted surgically. “Transcranial temporal interference stimulation” (tTIS) is a relatively new, noninvasive, and complementary approach. This technique stimulates deep brain regions without surgery, using electrodes that are temporarily attached to the scalp. We would like to investigate the effects of repeated tTIS on motor skills in patients with Parkinson’s disease while they are performing a playful virtual task, to better understand the underlying mechanisms and effect.

interventions.name: In patients with Parkinson's disease, the putamen is stimulated using transcranial temporal interference stimulation in repeated sessions and then using sham stimulation in repeated sessions while the patients are playing virtual table tennis, and the MDS-UPDRS Part III is conducted before and after

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-To participate in this study, you must be a native German speaker or have sufficient knowledge of German
-Diagnosis of idiopathic Parkinson’s disease according to the MDS criteria
Exclusion criteria:
-Contraindications for transcutaneous, noninvasive electrical brain stimulation
-Contraindications for MRI imaging
-Pre-existing conditions, that may significantly influence the results of MDS-UPDRS Part III, regardless of Parkinson’s symptoms
-MoCA < 18 points
